coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: One English search: no Mongolian rule found that specifically covers household employers or domestic workers. Labour Law 2021 (in force 2022) applies to formal and informal work; the ILO issued 10 standard employment-contract templates in Dec 2024 (not checked whether one covers domestic work). Social insurance is mandatory for employees. Nothing new beyond K06 (payroll/social insurance rejected).

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: One Mongolian-language search returned only Kazakhstan/UK results. No Mongolian scrap-metal licensing or register found. Last search only surfaced a buyer advert (dmp.mn). Unverified whether any register exists.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Pawnbrokers already covered by K03. Second-hand dealers: no register found. Only related fact: Ulaanbaatar stopped issuing UB plates to vehicles over 10 years old from 2025-06-01 (ikon.mn/n/3bx6), affects used-car trade but is not a recurring duty.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K13. The money-changer/gold-dealer search returned only Mongolbank gold-purchase and price news.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No adopted end-of-life-vehicle rule found. A UN-PAGE document proposes an importer-fee fund and authorised dismantlers for Mongolia (a proposal, date not confirmed). Watch item only.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: No new 2025 animal-health law found. Law on Animal Health amended 2023-12-08, 2024-06-05 and 2024-12-08 (international veterinary certificate definitions, per FAOLEX snippet). Livestock registration is run by aimag food/agriculture offices. Nothing new beyond K12.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: No abattoir or butcher licensing detail found. Only a 2025 Ulaanbaatar impact assessment of the Food Law on the parliament law forum (unopened). Nothing new.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No search spent; budget used on higher-priority categories.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Soum vet units are K11 (rejected). Animal medicine import/production licences sit with the agriculture ministry (per a draft medicine-law snippet); retail vet pharmacy rules not found.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Water Law art. 28 requires a water-use permit with a resource report, daily volume and an EIA; water-resource fee set by Gov. Res. 326 (2013), amended 2022 Res. 416, varies by river basin. Drilling-contractor registration not found.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Hazardous-waste carriers, collectors, recyclers and generators have a licence regime (Order A/18, 2018) and a 2025 register form plus consignment note (Order A/68, 2025-02-11). Non-hazardous haulers: nothing found. Septic haulers: nothing found.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Two searches and one fetch gave no usable result. The page fetched (legalinfo.mn/mn/detail/9555) was a 2006 energy-ministry electrical-equipment operating rule, not lift/boiler rules. Unverified.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: No search spent; budget.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Plant-protection chemicals need a non-automatic import licence from the agriculture ministry (WTO notification, HS 3808.91-93). A 2023 joint order (A/34, A/43, A/50) lists approved pesticides. Retail dealer or applicator reporting not found. Importers are few.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Outbound/inbound placement needs a licence from the labour minister (law of 2001). Foreign hires: a vacancy must be posted on the employment registry and, for grades 9-12, 14 working days must pass before an invitation can be requested. 2001 law reported as outdated and under redraft.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: About 40 licensed funeral firms, mostly in Ulaanbaatar; standards MNS6841:2020 and MNS5605:2006 (Thanos magazine 4/2024). Licensing authority and statute not identified.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: NGO law requires reporting to the registry and removal if re-registration is missed. Drafts exist for laws on associations and foundations, not confirmed as adopted. No halal certification scheme found.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Taxi licensing started 2024-10-15 (fee MNT 3-10M, eight requirements, per ikon.mn snippet). Ulaanbaatar has 5 taxi companies with 221 permits and a 2025-12 plan for a 1,000-car PPP taxi scheme (ikon.mn/n/3ke2, fetched). Bus fleets are on city e-payment/GPS run by the city. Truck/minibus duties not found.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: One search for money-changer licensing returned nothing on point. No vendor register found. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Driving schools: about 400 in 2022, registered under Road Traffic Safety Law art. 14. Childminding: rules on a service database in the education information system. Hunting outfitters: annual permits via public auction; 2026 argali quota 103. Tattoo studios and small food producers: nothing found.

coverage.found: The FRC licenses and supervises savings and credit co-operatives (SCC Law 2011, amended 4 times, a rewrite as a 'Financial Co-operatives Law' is in draft). One candidate recorded (C-B). The FRC reporting forms and the number of SCCs were not confirmed.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: The HIF (ЭМДЕГ) contracts 2,398 providers. From 2025 it sets monthly spending caps; private hospitals say they used up their 2025 funding by August and are owed about MNT 543bn. coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: The Law on Offences was amended on 2026-07-03, so Labour Law violations now number 16 types (7 new). No security or manpower agency register found. Only a generic HR-compliance lead (C-G), which is excluded as generic.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: 140 holders of common-minerals (sand, gravel, brick clay, building stone) use licences in Ulaanbaatar alone. coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Real estate brokerage is a licensed activity under the FRC; per a GRATA legal alert the 2020 FRC licensing procedure (Resolution 120) was replaced by FRC Resolution 648 of 2024-12-27 (reported by the search tool, not read directly). coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No beekeeper registration, licence or recurring filing regime found; a Mongolian honey export protocol or GACC honey registration was not found either (China's rules require sanitary registration of honey processors, not apiaries; Kyrgyz case needed a vet-service register, not Mongolian). Sector is small: Selenge aimag alone has 310 individuals and 9 firms with 6,656 colonies and 130+ t honey (Montsame, May 2025); a honey cluster NGO targeted 20 t/yr exports. Buyers are few, scattered and low-margin, and no mandatory duty found. Nothing new beyond the weak candidate below.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Water Law (Usny tukhai) requires water-use contracts/permits (permit tiers by m3/day: opinion needed above 100 m3/day, 50-100 m3 via aimag environment office), well passports and registration in the water database (Art 27.3), metering of every intake with verified meters (Metering procedure), and water accounting reports (Water Accounting procedure). Drinking-water standard MNS 0900:2018. Water Agency tested 19 bottled waters in 2024 (16 minor deviations, quarterly retesting announced). Urban water is run by state utilities (e.g. USUG lab with 23 staff). No soum-level small-system licence regime or software gap confirmed. One weak candidate below.

result.reason: Duty is partly confirmed. legalinfo.mn/mn/detail/13192 shows the 2018 forms order (A/21, 2 Feb 2018, not A/18) approved a hazardous-waste consignment note, an entity register and periodic reports for generators, transporters, collectors, recyclers and exporters. The page says A/68 of 11 Feb 2025 invalidates it. I did not open A/68's own text. That page does not state frequency, penalty or any e-filing system. Two searches found no software or state e-portal for hazardous-waste filing, so competition is unchecked rather than absent. Market size is not found. The licensed collectors are few, and small generators are diffuse with weak enforcement. That makes buyers hard to reach and willingness to pay low. Not tested: A/68's text, any penalty, the number of registrants, and whether filing is on paper.

Duty is real: the Labour Migration Law (in force 1 Jul 2022) requires an invitation approval and work permit from the labour authority. The 14-day vacancy-posting wait comes from PwC's 2022 summary and was not re-verified as current. Manpower agencies need a licence under the Law on Licensing. But this is an episodic, per-hire task, not a fixed recurring filing. The 2026 quota (Resolution 113) leaves most sectors unrestricted. The permit process appears to run on state electronic systems, which would limit room for a product, though e-Mongolia coverage is unconfirmed. I found no agency count and ran no competitor search. Buyers are few, and hiring firms are often large. Weak recurring-pain fit.

result.competitor: None found; competitor search returned nothing relevant for Mongolia
result.duty: Permit from the labour ministry's training institute (Road Traffic Safety Law 14.5-14.6): 1-year initial, 2-year renewal, requires own driving range; inspections aimed at every 6 months (2022 article, unconfirmed as current)
result.market: About 400 driver-training organisations in 2022 (154 in Ulaanbaatar, 175 rural, 55 professional schools)
result.reason: The only source is a 2022 ikon.mn article, now marked outdated. It says about 400 driver-training organisations hold permits issued by the labour ministry's training institute under Road Traffic Safety Law art. 14.5-14.6. Initial permits last 1 year and renewals 2 years. It says the ministry aims to inspect every 6 months, though the 2022 inspection was postponed. The duty is therefore a permit renewal roughly every 2 years plus occasional inspections. That is infrequent, with no reporting workflow. I found no 2025-26 confirmation of current rules, no penalty, and no competitor or software. Searches returned mostly irrelevant results. The market is small, about 400 firms. Low frequency and an unclear duty keep the score low.

Duty partly confirmed: Gratanet says the FRC approved the licensing procedure for real estate brokerage by Resolution 120 of 2020-03-11, as part of AML/CFT. I could not confirm that Resolution 648 of 2024 replaced it. I could not read the FIU broker guide (PDF unreadable), so report types, deadlines and penalties are unchecked. Broker count is not found; the FRC publishes a licensee list, but I did not see it. I found no broker-specific product or whether the FIU portal covers the filing. The market is likely a few dozen to a few hundred firms, with low reporting frequency, which means weak recurring pain and a small, hard-to-reach buyer pool. Keep a low score.
